issues.finding: Previously inventoried password bytes escape in the next document observation. Independent Chromium probe first observes a password field, then navigates to a page whose button echoes that value: firstContains=false, secondContains=true. The exported name/locator can enter the backend observation and future model context.
issues.suggested_action: Retain a bounded session-private masking inventory across observations and document replacement, including known sensitive/input/source bytes and normalized aliases; clear it only at confirmed teardown. Add process/callback canary tests for uncaptured password and ordinary input echoes on subsequent documents and after removal in the same document. No raw inventory may become public IPC, callback, diagnostic or manifest data.

issues.finding: Native check/uncheck reports success without verifying the requested checked state. A checkbox onclick preventDefault leaves checked=false after check; uncheck on a checked radio leaves checked=true. Both invoke calls return successfully, so GuidedRuntime emits SUCCEEDED/OK even though the typed operation did not complete.
issues.suggested_action: Check the actual postcondition on the retained original element after the single native attempt, without re-resolving or retrying. Reject inherently unsupported native uncheck targets before effects. After an effect has begun, preserve honest failure/uncertainty if state or identity cannot be confirmed. Add independent receipt/state tests for prevented toggles, radio targets, handlers that revert state, no-op and no second attempt.

issues.finding: Wire/auth parsing is not consistently closed. Real mTLS runner /assign accepts duplicate schemaVersion keys and reaches the claim port. GuidedContracts.parse accepts a second trailing JSON object. The Java JWT verifier accepts an unknown signed claim that the Node verifier rejects.
issues.suggested_action: Use duplicate-key rejecting, trailing-data rejecting and fatal UTF-8 JSON parsing on each applicable wire boundary, and agree/enforce the same closed JWT claim set and integer policy in Java/Node. Add malformed raw-byte transport tests rather than only validating already-parsed objects.

issues.finding: Custom runner date-time validation differs from the frozen schema validators: 2026-10-08T24:00:00Z is accepted by runner assignment validation but rejected by Java and Ajv. Runner also rejects the leap-second form accepted by the Ajv contract oracle. The custom resolver silently substitutes an empty schema for an unresolved definition and does not detect unsupported validation keywords.
issues.suggested_action: Establish tested Java/Node parity for the currently enforced wire schemas, including date-time edge cases. Validate the schema subset at load time and reject unresolved references/pointers or unsupported validation keywords. No OBS-006 learned-plan runtime support is demanded by this finding.

trace.given_when_then: Given valid assignment, worker credentials and frozen tuple, when claim/context/renew run over mTLS, then actual owner establishes and retains a bounded isolated worker; mismatched scopes/tuples refuse. SEC-002/REL-002 expose validation parity gaps.

Given retained current DOM identity, prepared operations refuse replacements and stale generations; real refresh continues between source steps. Given a prevented checkbox click or checked radio uncheck, however, invocation incorrectly succeeds with wrong final state (REL-001).

Given positively classified visible text/control source, admitted read captures exact whitespace bytes and an opaque handle; hidden/sensitive/stale/wrong-policy and blank/oversize reads refuse. The separate export privacy guarantee fails under SEC-001.
Given local producer success, only earlier same-origin authorized slots consume exact retained bytes; missing/replanned-away allocation, limits and cancellation refuse; sessions do not share values.

Given simultaneous/repeated dispatch or consume/send/ack failure, one committed winner and fsynced local consumption permit at most one attempt; unknown outcomes do not retry; cancel/expiry revoke and require confirmed browser cleanup.

Given a password privately inventoried on one page, when the next page echoes it as a button caption, then sanitized observation exports those bytes (SEC-001). Existing data-free receipts/process launch tests remain passing but insufficient.
